newsitem.title: USA: Stewart says mortgage rates won't hurt it.
newsitem.headline: Stewart says mortgage rates won't hurt it.

text.p: Stewart Information Services Corp said Wednesday that mortgage rates near the present level should not have a dramatic effect on its business.

"While the outlook for the rest of 1997 is less certain following recent Federal Reserve actions to raise interest rates, mortgage interest rates near the current level should not have a dramatic effect on our business," Carloss Morris, chairman and co-chief executive, said in a statement.
Higher interest rates would dampen demand for housing and could hurt results, while lower interest rates could improve results, Max Crisp, vice president of finance, said.
Rates that are pretty close to unchanged from the present level would not dramatically affect the business, Crisp said.
Order activity is trending up, with orders in April comparable to those of April 1996, Stewart said.
Among the reasons for the rising orders are Stewart's increasing share of the national title insurance market and growing participation in the commercial market segment, the company said.
The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates on March 25.
